subject: Inference deployment fit — recap, pain points, and next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Aurelia Tsai <aurelia.tsai@quantixlabs.com>, James Rowe <james.rowe@quantixlabs.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Inference deployment fit — recap, pain points, and next steps

Hi Aurelia / James,

Great meeting today — thanks for walking us through Quantix's ingestion pipeline and latency targets. Below is a short recap so we all have the same list of priorities and the immediate next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level goals we heard
- Serve real-time prompts for knowledge retrieval use case with P95 inference latency <= 120ms for short-context queries (<= 512 tokens).
- Predictable throughput of ~400 QPS during peak trading windows, with sustained bursts to ~900 QPS for 3–7 minute windows.
- Strong data isolation: model inference on a dedicated GPU pool with customer-level isolation and no shared KV persistence across tenants.

Current stack
- Frontend: Go microservices behind ALB in us-west-2.
- Vector DB: self-managed Vespa cluster (on-prem) for nearest-neighbor retrieval.
- Model experiments: evaluating a custom-tuned 13B open model running on mixed-precision.

Pain points / constraints
- Unreliable batching currently causing high tail latency during bursts.
- Procurement requires a firm SLA for latency + clear audit logs for model inputs/outputs (security/compliance team asked).
- On-prem footprint is limited; prefer Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering or a private deployment variant.

Success criteria (Quantix will consider this a fit if)
1) We can commit to a predictable P95 latency SLA at target QPS.
2) Isolation and audit log export meets their compliance checklist.
3) Seamless routing/fallback so availability is maintained if a reserved pool is saturated.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Dev/Marcus: brief technical sizing & recommended GPU pool configuration for the 400 QPS baseline and 900 QPS burst (need CPU/GPU, mem, and expected token-length distribution). Target: 2026-10-19 EOD.
- Stephanie: draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) and share a sample SLA + audit log export format. Target: 2026-10-19 morning.
- Aurelia/James: share an anonymized sample request profile (token length histogram and QPS by minute for a typical peak day).

Attachments: small architecture sketch I captured during the call (quantix-arch-sketch.png). I attached a blank MAP template that Ill prefill after Dev's sizing.

Thanks again — I think theres a strong fit here.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Aurelia Tsai <aurelia.tsai@quantixlabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: James Rowe <james.rowe@quantixlabs.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:10:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference deployment fit — recap, pain points, and next steps

Thanks Stephanie — this is great and captures everything we discussed. A couple of small clarifications:

- The 400 QPS baseline is an operational average across our US trading window; the 900 QPS bursts are extremely spiky (often < 5 minutes) but frequent during earnings.
- For compliance, we need per-request replayable logs (unredacted payloads) retained for 90 days and exportable via S3 or a secure FTP.
- Wed like to see a cost estimate for both Dedicated (reserved pools) and a private VPC-hosted option for comparison.

We will upload a 24-hour sample traffic trace in anonymized form to the Drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

Aurelia
Head of Platform Engineering, Quantix Labs
aurelia.tsai@quantixlabs.com

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 07:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Inference deployment fit — technical sizing ask

Stephanie / Marcus — quick internal note after reviewing the notes and Aurelia's clarifications. A few items Im going to size and validate with benchmarks:

1) Baseline 400 QPS (P95 <= 120ms): likely needs a mixed pool of A10G-like instances with batching tuned to average token length ~60–90 tokens. I suspect ~6 GPU units with continuous batching and prefix caching could satisfy baseline.
2) Bursts to 900 QPS: we should propose a burst pool with autoscaling policy that brings up additional GPUs within 30–45s and a faster fallback variant (quantized 8-bit) for extreme tail traffic.
3) Isolation: recommend dedicated tenant pools plus per-tenant storage encryption and S3-compatible audit export. We'll include how KV cache is purged on pool switches to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Ill run a short synthetic to estimate token/sec and memory per GPU and have a spreadsheet with numbers by EOD. Attaching the initial sketch I used when thinking through compute (quantix-arch-sketch.png).

-Dev

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Aurelia Tsai <aurelia.tsai@quantixlabs.com>, James Rowe <james.rowe@quantixlabs.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference deployment fit — recap, pain points, and next steps

Aurelia / James,

Thanks for the quick confirmation and for committing to the sample trace. Quick update on actions:

- Dev attached his initial sizing notes; weve scoped two options — Reserved Dedicated Pool (recommended for strict isolation + lowest sustained unit cost) and Private VPC deployment (recommended if you need the inference control plane in your network). Ill populate a short MAP and include a side-by-side cost / SLA summary.
- For audit logs: we can export per-request raw logs to your S3 bucket; retention policy is configurable and supports 90 days. We will include an example export file format in the MAP.
- Proposed timeline:
  * 2026-10-19: share MAP and cost sketches (Stephanie)
  * 2026-10-21: technical deep-dive with Quantix infra + security (Dev + Marcus)
  * 2026-10-25: procurement/contract intro and sample SLA (Sales ops / Legal)

Attachments: MAP-Quantix-2026-10-19.pdf (draft), quantix-arch-sketch.png (sketch).

If that looks good, can we pencil the deep-dive for 2026-10-21 10:00 AM PT?

Best,
